answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a fixed bond for 30 days before bidding for work. A thousand fake sellers therefore require a thousand bonds, tying up capital even if none wins a contract. Splitting identities cannot multiply access for free: the attacker pays the financing cost of every bond. Like bees seeking nectar at dawn, fake agents may swarm, but even a comet of new accounts must bring capital proportional to its size.
